interest: Iran asked the U.S. for Japan's and Korea's flags in 1949; a Tehran despatch is datelined 'Tokyo, Iran.'
overview: Iran's 1949 request via Embassy Tehran for Japan's and Korea's flags; State replied Japan's flag was unchanged and sent a Korean flag sketch. Includes a misfiled 1948 Marshall telegram on the National Public Service Law.

people.name: K. O'Shaughnessy
people.role: Foreign Service Officer / Drafting Officer, American Embassy, Tehran

subfiles.about: The American Embassy in Tehran transmits a request from the Imperial Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran for copies or images of the national flags of Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: Embassy Tehran forwards Iran's request for the national flags of Japan and Korea, which local U.S. offices lacked; the dateline reads 'Tokyo, Iran.'
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 190 from Embassy Tehran on Iranian Request for Flags of Japan and Korea

subfiles.about: The Department of State advises the American Mission in Tehran that Japan's national flag remains unchanged and transmits a sketch of the new Korean flag.
subfiles.summary: State tells the Tehran mission Japan's flag is unchanged since the war and encloses a sketch of Korea's new flag for Iran.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 65 from Department of State to American Mission, Tehran Regarding Flags of Japan and Korea
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge of the American Mission, Tehran

subfiles.about: Secretary of State Marshall requests independent reporting and documentation from the Political Adviser in Tokyo regarding the revision of Japan's National Public Service Law.
subfiles.from: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Marshall asks POLAD Tokyo for independent reporting on revision of Japan's National Public Service Law, including Cabinet orders and Japanese reactions.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Secretary of State Marshall to POLAD Tokyo Regarding Revision of National Public Service Law
subfiles.to: U.S. Political Adviser to SCAP (POLAD), Tokyo
